say: Welcome to the money shop! Today we pay with coins and notes, find every way to make an amount, and make sure we do not miss any and do not count the same way twice.
Here are three price tags in cents: an eraser 65¢, a pencil 80¢ and a sticker 30¢. Pick one and pay exactly with your play coins. Any way that pays exactly is a good way.
Now look for a way that uses fewer coins. How many coins did you use? Tell your partner.
How many different ways do you think there are to make 20¢ with 20¢, 10¢ and 5¢ coins? Write a guess.
stuck: Stuck: start with the biggest coin that fits, then fill the rest.
Not sure if two ways are different: “Same coins in a different order is the same way.”
For pairs who want more: find the ways to make 30¢. How will you know you have them all?

say: “Ways to make 15¢ with 10¢ and 5¢ coins. I start with the biggest coin: one 10¢. Then 5¢ is left, so one 5¢ coin. That is one way: 10 + 5.”
“Now no 10¢ coin. Only 5¢ coins: 5 + 5 + 5. That is two ways altogether.”
“25¢ with 20¢, 10¢ and 5¢: with a 20¢, 20 + 5. With 10¢ but no 20¢, 10 + 10 + 5 and 10 + 5 + 5 + 5. With only 5¢, 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5. That is 4 ways. I used a table so I did not repeat any.”

do: Ask: “What is your biggest coin in this way?”
Ask: “Are these two ways the same? Show me with coins.”
Ask: “How do you know there are no more ways?”
stuck: Hint 2: “Keep one coin fixed and change the others.”
Hint 3: “Draw a table with a column for each coin.”

say: “How did you make sure you found every way?”
ask: “How did you make sure you found every way?”
Start with the biggest coin and work down in order. 10 + 5 + 5 and 5 + 10 + 5 use the same coins, so they are one way.

say: “A table helped you check. Inquirers check, and today you checked every way.”

l6-title.note: Objective: Find all the ways to make an amount, work systematically, and use reasoning to rule out cases. Materials: Play coins (5¢, 10¢, 20¢, 50¢), about 6 of each per pair, mini whiteboards. Online: Print the cut-out coin sheet at the back of the workbook, or use real coins at home. Time plan: opening 0 to 2, warm-up 2 to 8 (game 2 to 6, quick questions 6 to 8; ask questions 1 to 3, and 4 and 5 only if you are on time), sneak-peek puzzles 8 to 12, explore 12 to 26, teaching 26 to 36 (click to reveal each step and answer), brain break 36 to 40, worksheet 40 to 72 with short teaching before each page and a check-together slide after it (a 30-second stand-and-stretch reset after the page-1 check, taken from that slot; the last 4 minutes check page 2, after a 1-minute stand-up stretch), talk time 72 to 79, exit ticket 79 to 85, look-back 85 to 88, then flex time and goodbye 88 to 90 (this is the buffer: if you are behind, use it; do not start anything new). Think harder, Go further and the Investigation are for every child to choose, any time or at home. Nobody is told which page they should be on. SPINE: Today's tool is List every way. Write each way down, in order, so none is missed. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

l6-tool.note: SPINE: Show for about 20 seconds, inside the opening. Today's tool is List every way. Write each way down, in order, so none is missed. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

l6-warm1.note: Minutes 2 to 6. Money Shop, cents only. Hand out play coins (5¢, 10¢, 20¢, 50¢). Point to one item at a time: "The pencil costs 80¢. Pay exactly with your coins." Any way that pays exactly is a good way. Then ask: "Can you find a way with fewer coins?" Do not ask who used the fewest. Click to show one way with the fewest coins: Eraser 65¢ = 50¢ + 10¢ + 5¢ (3 coins). Pencil 80¢ = 50¢ + 20¢ + 10¢ (3 coins). Sticker 30¢ = 20¢ + 10¢ (2 coins). Dollars are not needed today: they are on the Think harder page.

l6-warm2.note: Minutes 6 to 8. Children show the coins with play money, then click to reveal. Ask: "Could you pay 40¢ with two coins another way?" (no: only 20¢ + 20¢). Ask questions 1 to 3. Ask 4 and 5 only if the clock at minute 6 is on time. The 4-minute sneak-peek puzzles follow on the next slide.

l6-warmcheck.note: Minutes 8 to 12 (4 minutes). SAY (about 26 words, once): "Two sneak-peek puzzles: ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start, and I do not know is welcome. Nobody is marked." Question 1 is an access question: every child can try it with objects, a drawing or counting, so everyone starts with a win. Question 2 makes you think. Children try both on their own paper (about a minute each). Then everyone answers ONCE, after the second question: face to face, each child keeps the paper low so only the tutor sees it; online, children say the answers together on three (nothing is held up to the camera). There are no private chat messages. Never use boards or paper held up in front of the group or to the camera, and never read out or compare anyone's answer. Do not write scores down or announce them. Then click to show each answer to the whole group and say "Lots of us had a different idea, and that is fine." Look for good ideas to praise in a later lesson; do not keep a list of who found question 2 easy. When the worksheet starts (minute 40) invite the WHOLE group (“When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation”), never one child by name. Everyone joins Explore and the Mini-lesson. Answers: 1) Yes: 20¢ + 5¢. 2) 10¢ + 5¢, and 5¢ + 5¢ + 5¢. Those are the only two ways.

l6-explore1.note: Minutes 12 to 17. Pairs work with the materials: Play coins (5¢, 10¢, 20¢, 50¢), about 6 of each per pair, mini whiteboards. Pairs make 20¢ in as many ways as they can with 20¢, 10¢ and 5¢ coins, recording each on a whiteboard. Online: Print the cut-out coin sheet at the back of the workbook, or use real coins at home. Go further (what-if) is on this slide from the start: any pair may choose it at any time, so nobody waits. The tutor does not choose who and does not announce it. Answers: 6 ways: 20+10; 20+5+5; 10+10+10; 10+10+5+5; 10+5+5+5+5; six 5¢. Start with the biggest coin and work down.

l6-explore2.note: Minutes 17 to 26. Let pairs keep working and move around the room (or breakout rooms). Gather them to answer these. Answers: 1) 4 ways with 20¢, 10¢ and 5¢ coins. 2) Start with the biggest coin and work down. 3) No. The same coins, in a different order.

l6-teach1.note: Teach. Click to add each row while children say what goes in it. Think-aloud: "Ways to make 15¢ with 10¢ and 5¢ coins. I start with the biggest coin: one 10¢. Then 5¢ is left, so one 5¢. Now no 10¢: only 5¢ coins, three of them. The 10¢ column went 1, 0, so I know I am finished."

l6-we1.note: Click to build each row and the side notes. Ask before each row: "What comes next if I go one fewer?" Think-aloud: "With a 20¢: 20 + 5. With 10¢ but no 20¢: 10 + 10 + 5 and 10 + 5 + 5 + 5. With only 5¢: five of them. That is 4 ways. I used a table so I did not repeat any."

l6-try1.note: Own paper, ticked against the answer slide. a) 10, or 5 + 5. b) 10 + 10, 10 + 5 + 5, four 5¢. c) 20 + 5 + 5 + 5, or seven 5¢. Ask: "Why can't we use two 20¢ for c?" (40¢ is too much).

l6-try2.note: Own paper; say the answer together on three, then click. a) 10 + 5 = 15. b) 20 + 20 = 40 (the same coin twice is allowed). c) 50 + 5 = 55: start with the biggest coin that fits. These are the Question Bank Core items for Lesson 6, the same skill as worksheet Q3 and Q4.

l6-try3.note: Own paper; say the answer together on three, then click. a) 20, 30, 35: count on from the biggest coin. b) 20 + 20 = 40, then 45. Children who say 25¢ in b have added the numbers of coins. These are the Question Bank Core items 5 and 6, and prepare worksheet Q5 and Q6.

l6-key.note: Say the key idea together. Common mistakes to watch for during the worksheet: (1) Listing the same way twice in a different order (10+5+5 and 5+10+5). (2) Choosing many small coins instead of looking for the fewest. (3) Stopping at the first set in Think harder T2 instead of checking for all of them.

l6-break.note: Four minutes. Online: children stay in view of the camera and move in place.

l6-ws1.note: Minutes 40 to 52. Read questions 1 and 2 aloud. Walk around. Ask "How do you know you have them all?" Check that pairs work in order. Q1 has only 4 ways, so row E stays empty: that is fine. Q2 is the worked example from the Mini-lesson (25¢, 4 ways).

l6-ws1ans.note: Click after pairs explain. Q1c: "We started with the biggest coin and went one fewer each time until there were none." Q2: the same table as the worked example. Thirty cents (6 ways) is on the Think harder page (T4). Reset (about 30 seconds, taken from this slot): when the answers are checked, everyone stands, reaches up high, shakes out their hands, takes one slow breath and sits down again, then page 2. Skip it if you are more than a minute behind.

l6-teachfew.note: Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q3). Ask after step 3: "Could 2 coins make 65¢?" (No: the two biggest, 50 + 20, make 70, and no pair makes exactly 65.)

l6-teachnotes.note: Optional: dollars are now Think harder T5. Hold up play notes: "These are dollars, not cents. Look for the $ sign." Same idea as coins: biggest note that is not too much, then work down, then count on to check: 10, 20, 30, 35, 37, 38. Point out there is no $20 note, so $20 is two $10 notes. Watch for: children who mix up $50 and 50¢, and children who write 38¢ instead of $38.

l6-trynotes.note: Own paper, ticked against the answer slide. a) $10 + $2 + $2 (3 notes); $10 + $4 is not a note, so two $2 notes. b) Count on from $20 to $50: $30. c) $10 + $10 + $5 = $25, which is less than $27, so no: $2 short.

l6-ws2.note: Children work alone. Q5 and Q6 are short "count the money" items (Ali 20¢ + 10¢ + 5¢ = 35¢; Mei 20¢ + 20¢ + 5¢ = 45¢). Note who may need a short catch-up next lesson. Dollars are now on the Think harder page (T5), not on this page.

l6-ws2ans.note: Click after a child explains. Q5: 20, 30, 35. Q6: 20 + 20 = 40, then 45. Think harder T3 (Sam): six 10¢ = 60¢; each swap to a 20¢ adds 10¢; 30¢ more means 3 swaps. First, everyone stands up and stretches for about a minute (reach up high, touch your toes, shake out your hands) so there is some movement before talk time.

l6-stretch.note: For any pair that chooses to try more (these are on the slide only; Think harder T1 to T4 are in the workbook). Answers: 1) 9 ways (two 20¢: 1 way; one 20¢: 3 ways; no 20¢: 5 ways). 2) 2 ways: $10 + $1 + $1, and $5 + $5 + $2. 3) 4 coins: 50 + 20 + 20 + 5. Three coins cannot work: with a 50¢ coin you need 45¢ from two coins (no pair makes 45¢), and without it three coins make at most 60¢.

l6-teachexact.note: Optional teaching for any pair that chooses Think harder, before Think harder T2 (ALL the sets of 4 coins worth 70¢). Model trying every biggest-coin start, not stopping at the first answer.

l6-teachswap.note: Optional teaching for any pair that chooses Think harder, before Think harder T2 (Sam's 90¢). Act it out with play coins: lay out five 5¢, then swap one at a time and count the total aloud.

l6-challenge.note: For any pair that chooses Go further. Use it as a pair choice, or with volunteers in talk time (never call a child by name). Ask for the reason every time. Q3 is open: there is no single right answer, so ask children to check each other's work. Answers: 1) 15 different amounts: with 3 coins there are 7, and the 50¢ coin doubles that and adds one more. With a $1 coin as well there are 31: each new coin doubles the amounts and adds one more. 2) 2 sweets and 3 biscuits. 3) Open. A good puzzle has exactly one way. Example: 35¢ with exactly 3 coins from 5¢, 10¢, 20¢ and 50¢ has only 20¢ + 10¢ + 5¢. Check by listing every set of 3 coins.

l6-chdiag.note: Show this picture slide only if a pair asks for it, or is stuck on Go further. The pictures show each problem, not its answer. Ask: What do you notice? What do we know? What do we not know yet? Can you draw or build it? Do not point out the answer; wait for a child to find a pattern.

l6-chwalk.note: Use after pairs have tried. Reveal one answer at a time and ask a child to explain before you click. Many children stop at one answer: ask "Is there another way?" and "How do you know you found them all?" For Q3, ask two pairs to swap puzzles and solve each other's.

l6-talk.note: Minutes 72 to 79. Pairs talk for 2 minutes. Then ask for volunteers first ("Who would like to share?"), never call a child by name to answer, and say that passing is always fine. No tallies and no rankings. Praise the reasons, not only the answers.

l6-exit.note: Minutes 79 to 85. Answer: any correct way, for example 20¢ + 10¢, or 10¢ + 10¢ + 10¢, or 20¢ + 5¢ + 5¢. Extension: Make 50¢ in as many ways as possible using 5¢, 10¢, 20¢ and 50¢.

l6-reflect.note: SPINE: Minutes 85 to 88. Start the timer (120 seconds). Say: "Pick one problem from today. Question 1: did I answer the question? Question 2: does my answer make sense? Question 3: can I check it another way? Tick, write one line, or pass. If you are still stuck, tick the box and I will come." Children tick the Look back box on the Choose and look-back page of their workbook, or just tick on paper. A pass is always allowed. It is never marked, never collected in front of the group and never read out; the tutor may look at it afterwards. If a child ticks "I am still stuck", check in during the open session next lesson (a quick visit to the shared breakout room or a hand signal, with a parent nearby; never a direct message). Do not ask children to share. Praise a check you saw, not speed. Then stamp the journals. After the look-back, minutes 88 to 90 are flex time (the buffer): finish stamps, then goodbye. Do not start anything new.
